solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bird wanted from environs of Reeperbahn? German please, preferably

indicators.note: what is preferred comes first, so the German word is put ahead of the other piece

parts.note: bitte is the German word for please

indicators.note: the environs of a place are its edges, so take the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: A visitor to Hamburg's red-light district politely asks to be shown where a bird is wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reeperbahn is Hamburg's nightlife street, which steers the solver towards German; the outer letters give RN.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a wading marsh bird of the heron family, famous for its booming call.

clue.text: First point retracted (foot fault)

indicators.note: retracted means drawn back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: number one, No. 1, means first
a nub is a point or gist

explanation.surface: A tennis player is called for a first-point foot fault, later withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot fault' is a tennis term but here it is a fault of the foot itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful swelling on the joint of the big toe is a common deformity of the foot.

clue.text: Direction of alcoholic drinking whisky? AA offers such support

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the direction phrase holds the letter

parts.note: a heavy drinker heads to the pub, to bar
W is whisky in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An alcoholic drinking whisky is offered support by Alcoholics Anonymous.
explanation.walkthrough: AA suggests Alcoholics Anonymous but is the Automobile Association, the British breakdown service that tows cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakdown service tows vehicles, using a bar fitted behind a car to pull a trailer or another car.

clue.text: Later, arranged housing hunt here in London

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so the rearranged letters contain the search word
arranged means put in a new order, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: to scour is to hunt thoroughly

explanation.surface: Later, house-hunting is arranged in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Earls Court is a district of west London, once home to a big exhibition centre.

clue.text: Perfect 60s hairstyle reflected antiquated place

indicators.note: a reflection is reversed, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or perfect
a bun is a hairstyle, popular in the sixties

explanation.surface: A perfect sixties hairdo seen in a mirror looks old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is written AI, the 1 standing for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubia was an ancient region along the Nile in what is now Sudan and southern Egypt.

clue.text: Animal place to open

indicators.note: open here means opened out and rearranged, so the letters of the two words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Reads like an instruction about where to open an animal enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open' looks like a verb in the surface but signals the rearrangement of PLACE and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: The polecat is a dark-furred mammal of the weasel family, a European relative of the ferret.

clue.text: Nose contains no sun protection? It's temporary

indicators.note: contains places the following pieces inside the prying word

parts.note: to nose is to pry
O is zero, nothing
a visor shades the eyes from the sun

explanation.surface: Someone's nose has no protection from the sun, but the sunburn is only temporary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something provisional is arranged for the time being, so it is temporary.

clue.text: Coiffeur discards pen catalogue

indicators.note: discards means throws away, so the animal enclosure is taken out

parts.note: a coiffeur is a hairdresser, a stylist
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: A hairdresser throws away a pen and a catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like a writing tool but is a pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalogue is an itemised record, and an inventory of items is also a list.

clue.text: Which steel, ultimately in conflict, may pierce heart?

definitions.text: Which steel, ultimately in conflict, may pierce heart?

indicators.note: pierce means go through, so the pieces go inside the heart word

parts.note: the core is the heart of something

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word
in conflict means in turmoil, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Asks which steel weapon, in battle, might stab a man through the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'ultimately' takes the last letter of steel, and 'in conflict' scrambles the may to LAYM, all set inside the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish broadsword is a steel weapon wielded in battle that may run an enemy through.

clue.text: Ten rounds enthralling — everyone peripherally sees attribute of heavyweight?

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the shuffled letters hold the next word
rounds suggests the letters going round and changing order, a shuffle

parts.note: everyone means all

indicators.note: peripherally means at the edges, so take the outer letters

explanation.surface: Ten rounds of boxing grip everyone watching a heavyweight bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounds' reshuffles TEN into TNE to hold ALL. A heavyweight is a boxer, and great height is a feature of many.
explanation.definitionFit: Big boxers are often very tall, so great height is a physical characteristic of a heavyweight.

clue.text: More contemporary fleecy item available in navy backing

indicators.note: in places the woolly animal inside the reversed letters
backing means going backwards, so the navy's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
a ewe is a sheep, an animal with a fleece

explanation.surface: A shopper hunts for a modern fleece jacket in navy blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleecy item' suggests clothing, but it is a sheep; 'backing' turns RN into NR.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative meaning more recent or more up to date, matching more contemporary.

clue.text: Promotion features centrepiece of 'Dickens — The Complete Works'. Here?

indicators.note: features means includes, so the promotion word holds the next piece within it

parts.note: a boost is a promotion or publicity push

indicators.note: the centrepiece of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: the complete works are all of them, everything

explanation.surface: An advert for a complete Dickens set asks where it might be bought.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'Here?' leans on the whole clue: a place where a Dickens promotion of the complete works would be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand selling books is exactly where a set of an author's complete works would be promoted.

clue.text: Film actor having row about bog provided

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rowing word goes round the boggy ground

parts.note: to row a boat is to oar it, so oar stands for row
a marsh is boggy ground
provided that means if

explanation.surface: An actor quarrels over a toilet, if the conditions are right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' and 'bog' tempt the solver towards a quarrel and a lavatory (British slang); they are an oar and a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian star of Lawrence of Arabia and Doctor Zhivago was a celebrated screen actor.

clue.text: Record company pursued by new artist

indicators.note: pursued by means followed by, so the label comes first

parts.note: EMI is a well-known British record label

explanation.surface: A record label is chased by a fresh young artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracey Emin is a British conceptual artist, known for her installation My Bed.

clue.text: Athlete reaches peak, holding third place to measure pulse

parts.note: a runner is an athlete

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the peak holds the letter

parts.note: Ben is a Scottish mountain peak

indicators.note: the third place in the word means its third letter

explanation.surface: An athlete reaching a summit stops to take their pulse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' seems to be a heartbeat but is a seed vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are edible seeds of pod plants, and this climbing bean is one.

clue.text: Rode badly round Uttoxeter, veering primarily into racer's course

indicators.note: into says the inner build goes inside the racer word

parts.note: a racer's is read as a horse's, a racehorse being a racer

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters surround the initials
badly says the letters of the riding word are scrambled
primarily means take the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A jockey rides poorly at Uttoxeter, swerving onto the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' scrambles the riding word to DOER, around the initials; Uttoxeter is an English racecourse, and 'course' is the menu sense, not the track.
explanation.definitionFit: Starters served before the main dish make up a course of a meal.

clue.text: Sportsman to economise when eating — just half King Edward?

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the economising word encloses the half word

parts.note: to skimp is to economise

indicators.note: half says take the first half of the word

parts.note: ER is Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A sportsman saves money by eating just half a King Edward, a potato variety.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a British potato variety, matching 'eating'; here it is the royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who competes by leaping from a ramp on skis is a sportsman.

clue.text: For booze at do, Cava's ordered

indicators.note: ordered means put into an arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter, so the Spanish sparkling wine's name is used as written

explanation.surface: Someone orders cava at a party for drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like requested at the bar, but it signals the reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Advocaat is a Dutch egg-and-brandy liqueur, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Element in cricket match periodically attempt to transgress

parts.note: a cricket match is made up of overs, sets of six balls

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so take every other letter

explanation.surface: Someone tries now and then to break the rules of a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of ATTEMPT give TEP; an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To go beyond a set limit is to break bounds, and to break bounds is to transgress.

clue.text: Frogman, for your information, takes part in talk. What struggling workers are doing?

parts.note: a frogman is an underwater diver

indicators.note: takes part in places the abbreviation inside the talking word

parts.note: to sing is slang for talking to the police

explanation.surface: A diver joins in a conversation about how hard-pressed workers are managing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: workers who are struggling might be branching out into other work.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking on new kinds of work or business is a way of broadening out, something those in difficulty may try.

clue.text: Dip into investment account upset ex-tennis player

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read from the bottom up
into puts the dip word inside the account

parts.note: an ISA is a British individual savings account
to sag is to dip

explanation.surface: A retired tennis player is upset at dipping into savings.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a British tax-free savings account; 'upset' reverses ISSAGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre Agassi is a retired American tennis champion, an eight-time Grand Slam winner.

clue.text: Latest ones to daub factor 11 for a Parisian tan

indicators.note: the latest ones are the last letters of each word

parts.note: onze is French for eleven

explanation.surface: The newest sunscreens are applied with low factor 11 for a French tan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'factor 11' suggests sun cream, but factor is just a source of its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A brownish metallic colour describes skin darkened by the sun.

clue.text: Rejected some dark oven-ready vegetable

indicators.note: Rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cook throws out a vegetable that was ready for the oven but had gone dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra, also called ladies' fingers, is a green podded plant eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Move fake by artist, in hindsight. 'Whistler' that's perching in the room?

parts.note: to budge is to move
to rig is to fake or fix

indicators.note: hindsight looks back, so the artist's letters are read backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A forged painting is moved, and Whistler the painter is pictured hanging in the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistler' suggests the American painter, in keeping with 'artist' and 'fake'; it is a bird that whistles, perched in a cage indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: The budgie is a small chirping parrot often kept indoors on a cage perch as a pet.

clue.text: Waffles producing much flatulence

definitions.meaning: waffles means talks idly at length, chatters
breaking wind repeatedly, emitting a lot of wind

explanation.surface: Breakfast waffles cause wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to prattle on and to emit wind.

clue.text: Cold place to park dope

parts.note: C is cold on taps
a lot is a car park, especially in America

explanation.surface: A cold car park is a place to buy drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' looks like drugs but means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms for a foolish person: an idiot or a dope, British informal usage.

clue.text: Dec publicises courtship openly, whereas his partner ___. Horny creatures

parts.note: Dec's partner is Ant, of the TV presenting pair Ant and Dec
the contrast with whereas asks for the opposite of a public courtship: running off secretly to marry

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank about a TV duo: one courts in public while the other runs off secretly.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a British TV presenting double act; the blank is filled by what Ant does, set against Dec's openness.
explanation.definitionFit: These grazing animals carry horns, so horny creatures is a playful description of them.

clue.text: Perfume, rearmost couple declined, that's quite close to Cologne

indicators.note: the last two letters are refused, so they are removed from the end

parts.note: essence is a perfume or scent

explanation.surface: A perfume is turned down by the last couple, being too close to eau de Cologne.
explanation.walkthrough: Cologne suggests the scent, matching 'Perfume', but here it is the German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is a city in Germany's Ruhr region, not far north of the city of Cologne.

clue.text: Centre for ski-trips safeguards piste after avalanche one forecasts

indicators.note: safeguards means holds protectively, so the middle letters go round the rearranged slope
the centre of a word is its middle letters
after an avalanche a slope is churned up, so its letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A skiing tour guide protects the slope after a snowslide and predicts conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after avalanche' jumbles the ski slope into IPSTE, which the middle pair of letters then wraps; a tipster is the tout giving racing predictions.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gives tips on likely winners, especially in racing, predicts outcomes for others.

clue.text: Single, surrounded by flighty nurses — time for a lark?

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the single letter inside the rearranged letters
flighty means unsettled, so the letters move around

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, single

explanation.surface: A single man is surrounded by giddy nurses, a moment for some fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lark' looks like a prank; it is the bird, whose song greets the dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The skylark sings at dawn, so daybreak is its time; early risers are called larks.
